headline: Belagavi reports highest severe child stunting in Karnataka with 50,522 affected children at anganwadis
summary: Belagavi district recorded the highest number of severely stunted children in Karnataka, with 50,522 cases identified among children registered at anganwadi centres, according to data tabled in the Legislature in February 2026. Despite multiple state nutrition programmes, the district faces persistent malnutrition challenges. Research from urban slums reveals local determinants of undernutrition, while grassroots organizations document awareness gaps and system failures. The district also faces concerning teenage pregnancy rates and child marriage cases that compound maternal-child health vulnerabilities.

modelFactorWhy.why: The pages discuss anganwadi coverage and nutrition programmes for young children but contain no specific data about school enrollment rates for children aged 3-6 in Belagavi district.
modelFactorWhy.mechanism: Early childhood education provides structured nutrition support through mid-day meals and enables developmental monitoring that can prevent stunting

modelFactorWhy.factor: Mothers who took iron-folic acid for 180+ days in pregnancy
modelFactorWhy.why: While pages document maternal anemia as a concern in rural Belagavi and mention government healthcare programs, they provide no district-specific data on iron-folic acid supplementation compliance rates during pregnancy.
modelFactorWhy.mechanism: Adequate iron-folic acid intake during pregnancy prevents maternal anemia and low birth weight, both directly linked to childhood stunting
